title: The Roster Trap: Why Longer Christmas Trading Hours Don't Always Mean a More Profitable Retailer
linkedin:
Christmas rosters are locked in across retail this week. Longer trading hours, extra casual cover for Boxing Day and New Year's Day. It feels like an easy call heading into the biggest trading weeks of the year.

Here's the part most rosters don't account for.

Not every trading hour earns the same margin. The hours added to capture extra Christmas trade are usually the thinnest ones in the day, the early slot before school drop off or the stretch after most shoppers have gone home. Revenue from those hours is real. Whether it covers the wage cost of staffing them is a separate question.

Boxing Day and New Year's Day both carry public holiday penalty rates. Casual loading sits on top for anyone without guaranteed hours. Most retailers build this year's roster from last year's figures, adjusted for a few extra shifts, without checking whether award rates moved or whether last year's hours were ever actually profitable.

The gap between the roster that was planned and the wage bill that lands usually only shows up in the January pay run, well after the decisions that created it were made.

December revenue is the strongest month of the year for most retailers. A strong top line makes it easy to assume the result underneath is proportionally strong too. It isn't always.

The fix isn't complicated. Measure contribution margin per labour hour, by shift, not just total revenue for the month. Once that number exists, it's obvious which hours are carrying the result and which are being kept open out of habit.
